learning: Track 0.10 m is tested only with the ±0.04 m row and kp 3.0. Iteration 3 used 0.10 m only at kp 2.0 with the narrower row. If the result matches the baseline, geometry is exhausted for this controller and kd (about 0.2) is the next lever.
notes: Iteration 9 package: the ±0.04 m, 16 mm row at mass 0.8 kg with wheel_track 0.10 m, the only geometry change. Controller is the iteration-8 controller (kp 3.0, kd 0.05), so any change against iteration 8 comes from wheel_track.
rationale:
Iteration 8 (±0.04 m, 16 mm row at y = 0.07 m, kp 3.0, mass 0.8 kg, wheel_track 0.12 m) scored 36.3097 and matched iteration 6 to four decimals on all tracks. Widening the row removed no line loss, so the sensor reach is not the limit. Iteration 7 showed that mass 0.5 kg lowers the score, so mass stays at 0.8 kg. The only evidence that moves the score is kp 3.0, which helped on the slalom alone.

The Builder asks for one geometry change: wheel_track 0.12 m to 0.10 m on the ±0.04 m row. I keep the iteration-8 controller exactly (kp 3.0, ki 0, kd 0.05, base_speed 1.6, last_direction) so the result isolates wheel_track. The weights stay at (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2), the iteration-8 scaling (x/0.02). These match the earlier steering gain per metre, and the Builder's x/0.03 wording conflicts with the iteration-8 weights actually raced. I keep the iteration-8 weights so the comparison against score 36.3097 is clean. Iteration 3 showed that 0.10 m alone at kp 2.0 gave no change, so this test checks the kp 3.0 combination. The Builder expects the metrics to stay near baseline. I do not claim an outcome.

kd stays at 0.05 for this race. Changing kd now would confound the track test. If the metrics match the baseline, kd about 0.2 is the next controller test, aimed at the slalom oscillation of 0.16.
